title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make X and Y Equal
summary: Given two positive integers x and y, determine the least number of operations needed to make x equal to y.
statement: Given two positive integers x and y, determine the least number of operations needed to make x equal to y. Operations include dividing x by 11 if divisible, dividing by 5 if divisible, decrementing x by 1, or incrementing x by 1.
constraints: x and y are positive integers.
One move increments or decrements the current value, or divides it by five or eleven when exactly divisible.
Return the minimum moves needed to reach y.
hints: Before a division, the optimal path may adjust either down or up to the nearest multiple.
Memoize by current value and compare direct decrements with both rounding directions for divisors five and eleven.
For each divisor d, try r decrements then divide, or d-r increments then divide; stop with direct increments once value≤y.
Any path using a next division must first reach some multiple; the nearest multiple in either direction dominates farther ones before that same division, so the recurrence is exhaustive.
editorial: Any path using a next division must first reach some multiple; the nearest multiple in either direction dominates farther ones before that same division, so the recurrence is exhaustive.

tests.explanation: Decrement to twenty-five, then divide by five twice, for three moves.
Increment to fifty-five, divide by eleven and five, then increment to two, for four moves.
